plan.title: What your elements do to your look
Your colors, worked out from your chart
Your presence: rooms, photos, first meetings

strong.text:
Your chart is the strong kind, {dm_short}, so the aura described above arrives at full concentration, often before you've decided to send it. That's powerful at work and in crowds. Up close, it can feel like a lot. People sometimes hesitate before approaching you, not because they dislike you, but because you seem complete already, like you don't need anyone to join.

The strong-chart glow-up isn't dimming. It's adding an invitation. A relaxed face while you listen, an open posture, one soft or playful element in your look that says you're approachable. The aura stays exactly as strong. It just gets a door in it.

A quick way to test the door: notice how often people start conversations with you, rather than the other way round. If it's rare, they're admiring from a distance. Soften one thing at a time, your greeting, your stance, the first ten seconds of eye contact, and watch the number change within a month.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your aura arrives before you do. Add a door so people can come in.

weak.text:
That's your {dm_short} aura with a full battery. Your chart is the weak kind, so the battery drains faster than most: on good days people feel everything described above, and on tired days the same aura runs on low power and can get lost in loud rooms. You may have learned to rely on being liked rather than being noticed on those days. That works, and it also means people discover how interesting you are later than they should.

The weak-chart glow-up isn't turning into someone louder. It's keeping the battery charged and making the signal easier to pick up. Clothes that fit properly, a haircut that holds its shape, one detail people remember you by. Small structure makes a quiet aura carry across a room.

A quick way to test the amplifier: take a photo of yourself in what you wore today and look at it as if you were a stranger. Does it say anything about you? If it mostly says "didn't want to bother anyone," choose one detail tomorrow that says something specific, and repeat it until it becomes yours.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your aura is real, just quiet. Fit, haircut, one memorable detail. That's the amplifier.

base.aura: Your aura is tall-tree energy. Before you speak, people sense direction: this person knows where they're going and probably has a plan for getting there. Gap carries a clean, upright presence that reads as dependable and a little bit in charge. It's the aura of the friend everyone calls when the group trip falls apart. There's warmth in it, but it's structured warmth, like shade from a big tree on a hot day. Your glow isn't sparkle. It's steadiness that slowly makes people feel safer. When you're at your best, you look like someone who has grown into exactly the right shape. The glow-up for you isn't becoming someone softer or flashier. It's letting that natural backbone show without apologizing for how much space it takes.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Gap, your aura is pure tall-tree energy. People feel safe the second you walk in.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: They also feel like you're about to assign them a task.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Clean lines and good boots on you? Main character in a quiet K-drama.

spring.intro:
Spring is Wood's own season, {dm_short}, so you were born in season, with the element of your Day Master in full command. Your aura reads as fresh, upright and full of momentum. People sense someone who is going somewhere. The risk of so much growth energy is a look that never settles: always mid-project, a bit rushed, hair pushed back with a pen. Your glow-up is polish and edges, letting the growth look intentional. Cleaner lines, one tailored piece, a finish that says the tree chose its shape. Your palette chapter below shows exactly which colors do that for your chart.

One seasonal note: spring-born charts tend to glow brightest when life is moving. In slow, stuck stretches, change something small in your look, a new haircut, a different bag, and your energy usually follows.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Born in spring, in season. You look like momentum. Now make it look intentional.

summer.intro:
Summer is Fire's season, and Wood feeds Fire, so a summer-born {dm_short} was born out of season, giving energy away to the heat. Your aura reads as warm, generous and expressive, the person who lights up a table. It can also read as spent: you pour so much outward that your look ends up an afterthought, thrown on between plans for other people. Your glow-up is replenishment. Give your style the same care you give your friends. Fabrics that feel good, a haircut on a schedule, one thing you wear purely because you love it. The details follow in your palette chapter.

One seasonal note: summer-born charts tend to run hot and then crash. Build cooling-off time into your routine, early nights, quiet mornings, a slower week after a busy one. Your face shows rest faster than most.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You dress like someone who spent all their energy on other people. Because you did.

autumn.intro:
Autumn belongs to Metal, the element that cuts Wood, so an autumn-born {dm_short} was born out of season, a tree in the pruning months. Your aura reads as disciplined, serious, a little guarded, like someone who's been edited. People trust you quickly and approach you slowly. Your style may lean strict and safe. The glow-up is letting some growth back in: softer textures, a little movement in the fabric, an expression that relaxes before you speak. Pruned trees grow back beautifully. Your palette chapter shows which colors help that happen for your chart.

One seasonal note: autumn-born charts tend to edit hard, in their closets and their lives. Edit, but keep one indulgent piece around. Your aura needs a little softness to balance the precision.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Autumn pruned you a bit. Let something soft grow back into your look.

winter.intro:
Winter is Water's season, and Water feeds Wood, so a winter-born {dm_short} was born in season in the supporting sense: roots fed all through the cold months. Your aura reads as calm, deep and quietly capable, with more going on underneath than on top. That depth can come across as reserve, or even as hiding. Your style may be practical to the point of invisible. The glow-up is letting the spring show. A little more structure, a confident shape, one detail that tells people you've got plans. Your palette chapter spells out the colors.

One seasonal note: winter-born charts tend to retreat when tired and hide in layers. On low days, wear one thing that's light or bright in spirit. It pulls you out of hibernation faster than willpower.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Deep roots, invisible outfit. Let the top of the tree show a little.

earth.intro:
You were born in the Earth days at the end of a season, when Earth takes command. Wood controls Earth, so for a {dm_short} this is out of season: your roots had to push through packed ground. Your aura reads as determined and practical, the person who gets it done without fuss. It can also read as heavy or tired, like someone carrying more than their share. Your glow-up is lightness. Less bulk, more breathing room, clothes that move when you move. Your palette chapter shows which colors lift you.

One seasonal note: charts born in the Earth days tend to absorb other people's moods. Clear your space and your calendar regularly. A tidy room and a free evening do more for your glow than any product.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You grew through hard ground. Your look can be lighter than your load.

three-words.heading: Your aura in three words, and its shadow
three-words.text: Your aura in three words, Gap: upright, certain, protective. Its shadow in three more: rigid, impatient, closed. Same tree, different weather. On good days people feel sheltered near you. On tired days they feel blocked. The difference is rarely your clothes. It's whether your face and posture are open. Before an important meeting or date, take three slow breaths and drop your shoulders. The shelter comes back.

base.aura: Your aura is a wildflower growing through a crack in the pavement: lovely, adaptable and much tougher than it looks. Eul has a soft, approachable glow that makes people want to talk to you. You read as friendly, creative and easy to be around, the person strangers ask to take their photo because you look like you'd make them look good. There's movement in your energy, a lightness that changes shape depending on the room. That's your gift and your challenge. Your glow is at its brightest when it's clearly yours, not borrowed from whoever you're with. The glow-up for you is deepening the color of that flower, so people remember not just that you were lovely, but exactly who you were.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Eul, your aura is a wildflower. Soft, friendly, strangers instantly trust you.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: They also assume you'll agree with whatever they say. Do you?

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Soft drape and a delicate ring on you look like a garden café poster.

three-words.heading: Your aura in three words, and its shadow
three-words.text: Your aura in three words, Eul: graceful, adaptable, charming. Its shadow in three more: blurry, eager, borrowed. On good days you're the most delightful person in the room. On tired days you become a mirror for whoever's nearest. The difference is whether you've checked in with your own taste that day. Wear one thing each morning that you chose before asking anyone.

base.aura: You give off pure sunlight. Byeong walks in and the temperature rises, in the best way. People notice you even when you're not trying, and honestly, you're often trying a little. You radiate optimism, generosity and that "let's do something fun" energy that makes a boring night instantly better. Your glow is wide and open; it touches everyone in the room. That's why you're photographed at every party and remembered by people you met once. The glow-up for you isn't getting brighter. You're already very bright. It's learning to shine with depth, so people don't just see your warmth, they feel how genuine it is. Think golden hour rather than noon: the same sun, but richer, softer and far more beautiful to look at.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Byeong, your aura is sunshine. Every room gets warmer when you arrive.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: And louder. So much louder.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Rolled sleeves, open collar, big laugh? You were built for sunlight.

Your glow-up is editing. Let one thing be the focus and the rest support it. A fire with good fuel doesn't need to show it all in one go. The palette chapter covers the colors.

One seasonal note: spring-born charts tend to glow brightest when life is moving. In slow, stuck stretches, change something small in your look, a new haircut, a different bag, and your energy usually follows.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Spring fed your flame. You don't have to show all of it at once.

Your glow-up is contrast and calm. Something cool and steady beside the heat, one quiet day for every loud one. Your palette chapter tells you what brings the temperature down beautifully.

One seasonal note: summer-born charts tend to run hot and then crash. Build cooling-off time into your routine, early nights, quiet mornings, a slower week after a busy one. Your face shows rest faster than most.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Born in summer, in season. You're the sun at noon. Squinting is not attraction.

Rest, warmth and things that make you feel looked after show on your face faster than anything you can buy. Your palette chapter shows the colors that feed your flame.

One seasonal note: autumn-born charts tend to edit hard, in their closets and their lives. Edit, but keep one indulgent piece around. Your aura needs a little softness to balance the precision.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Autumn makes you work for your warmth. Feed the flame first, then dress it.

People find you comforting, and you may underrate how much. Your style might lean careful, layered, cautious. The glow-up is brightness with protection: one warm, confident element in every look, a face that's well rested, and a little less hiding under layers. Your palette chapter covers which colors keep the flame going.

One seasonal note: winter-born charts tend to retreat when tired and hide in layers. On low days, wear one thing that's light or bright in spirit. It pulls you out of hibernation faster than willpower.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Winter flame. You're the light in the window, dressed like the curtain.

One element in your look that's just for delight, and a little more of your own warmth kept for yourself. Your palette chapter shows the colors.

One seasonal note: charts born in the Earth days tend to absorb other people's moods. Clear your space and your calendar regularly. A tidy room and a free evening do more for your glow than any product.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You turned your warmth into ground for everyone. Keep a little spark for you.

three-words.heading: Your aura in three words, and its shadow
three-words.text: Your aura in three words, Byeong: radiant, generous, open. Its shadow in three more: loud, scattered, exhausting. On good days you warm everyone. On tired days you perform warmth you don't feel, and people sense the effort. The difference is rest. When you're truly rested, your glow needs no help at all.

base.aura: You give off candlelight. Not the stadium spotlight, the soft glow that makes a small room feel intimate and safe. Jeong carries a warm, focused, slightly mysterious energy. People feel drawn closer to you, often without knowing why, and once they're near, they feel understood. You have the kind of presence that makes strangers confide in you at a party at 1am. Your glow is detailed and personal: a thoughtful look, a perfect question, the feeling that you're truly paying attention. The glow-up for you isn't becoming louder to compete with brighter people. It's trusting that your quiet flame is magnetic exactly as it is, and letting more people see it instead of saving it only for a few.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Jeong, your aura is candlelight. People feel safe and seen around you.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: They also think you're shy. You're not shy. You're judging the lighting.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Velvet, cashmere, one heirloom ring. You look like a winter love song.

three-words.text: Your aura in three words, Jeong: tender, focused, intimate. Its shadow in three more: guarded, intense, withdrawn. On good days people feel seen by you. On tired days you go dim and private and nobody knows why. The difference is whether you've said what you feel lately. Saying it keeps the flame steady.

base.aura: The aura you carry is a mountain at sunrise: solid, calm and quietly impressive. Mu carries grounded, unhurried energy that makes people relax. In a chaotic room, you're the one who looks like nothing could knock you over, and people instinctively stand near you. You read as trustworthy, mature and reliable, the friend who'll still be here in ten years. Your glow isn't flashy. It's presence. You don't need to fill silence, and that confidence is magnetic in a world of over-talkers. The glow-up for you is letting people see the warmth and humor that live inside the mountain. Think of sunlight hitting the peak: the same rock, suddenly golden and beautiful to look at.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Mu, your aura is a mountain. Calm, solid, everyone relaxes next to you.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: They also can't tell if you're happy or quietly filing a complaint.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: A good wool coat and sturdy boots. You look effortlessly expensive.

When you tend to yourself as well as you tend to everyone else, the whole garden blooms.

base_panels.text: Gi, your aura is a garden. People feel at home with you in five minutes.

base_panels.text: Because you've already fed them, found them a charger and asked about their mom.
